simple.meaning: אֵלֶּה (ʼêlleh) is a Hebrew word meaning “these.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵלֶּה (H429) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֵלֶּה (H429) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֵלֶּה (ʼêlleh) / H429 is traced through Jeremiah 10:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H429. elleh אֵלֶּה demonstrative pronoun plural these (Nabataean אלה (Lzb 264 Cooke 241 ), Cappadocian and Egyptian Aramaic אלה (Lzb Eph. i. 323 RÉS 361A 3 S-C Pap. E.13, Ki 13 ): probably therefore not, as used to be supposed, a Hebraism, but a peculiarity of the dialects of Jer 10:11 and of Ezra (in which the usually Aramaic form אִלֵּין does not occur) : see further אִלֵּין ); — these , 10:11 ; Ezra 5:15 Kt.

occurrences.englishText: “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’ ”
